answer: One concrete Sybil defence is upfront bond pricing: an agent identity must lock collateral larger than any reward one account can extract, so N fake keys cost N bonds at once. New accounts sit at the nadir of trust and rise only through metered work, so a duplicate key earns nothing. Each identity also signs a unique, non-transferable quill of provenance bound to its collateral, blocking key reuse. At settlement capital moves to a jetty and stays frozen until grading closes, removing early withdrawal after cheap farming. Sybils must therefore fund every key and forfeit it on detection.
